Founding document · 1971 · signed by all five

The Charter of the Watch

We are not radio amateurs and we are not ghost hunters. We are listeners. The longwave band above Westridge carries traffic that does not appear in any registry, on a schedule that answers to nothing we can name. We do not claim to understand it. We claim only the discipline to witness it, honestly, in shifts, forever — because something on that band has been witnessing us first, and a watch that is only kept in one direction is not a watch at all.

Every operator signs the seven principles before their first night. They are not rules so much as conditions of survival on the dial. We print them here so that any future listener understands what they are agreeing to the moment they tune in.

  1. Hold the frequency. The carrier is never to be left unattended between dusk and first light.
  2. Log everything, especially the silence. Empty band is not empty; it is masked.
  3. Never answer a voice that uses your name before you have given it.
  4. The names of operators are always written under a shift. We do not record ourselves plainly.
  5. What the band returns to you is not a coincidence. Treat the repetition as a message.
  6. If the dial gives instructions, follow them slowly and verify each step before the next.
  7. The watch outlives the operator. When you can no longer keep it, leave the way in for the next listener.

Signed, in the relay shed, the first night of the cooperative: A. Holloway · M. Reyes · D. Okafor · S. Lindqvist · and one signature struck through.

Appended to the charter, in a later hand, is a single line the archivist could not interpret. It is preserved here exactly, encoded as it was found (it is ordinary text in base​64):

dGhlIGZyZXF1ZW5jeSBpcyAxNDc3MA==

Decoders welcome. The carrier confirms its own answers, if you are patient.
